doc.title: Dave Valentin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: How he composes
summary: He writes at the piano and is inspired by travel and life; tunes start from rhythm or melody.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you write at the piano?
Yeah. Before it was all by hand, now I have the computer so.
But yeah, everything on the piano.
But is it possible to describe what gets a tune started for you?

I think life. Life. Traveling. Going to Indonesia, going to Japan. Walking down the street. Smelling food. Anything can set me off. Traveling to Brazil. Just mental pictures. You come back with a lot of mental and good feelings, bad feelings.
Does it usually start with the melody end of things or with the rhythmic, maybe chordal?
Both ways. Sometimes I get some rhythmic stuff in my head and then the melody comes later, and then sometimes it’s just the melody and the rhythm comes later.
